_comment: Guided tour of the native PTO inspector. 'name' is the emtk control or window (the keys of PtoInspectorApp.rects); 'filename' is heard when a container has been opened, 'Verify' when the button is pressed. The Qt tool keeps guide.json.

steps.title: What a .pto is
steps.text: A .pto is one measurement in one file: the instrument file byte for byte, and every result computed from it beside it. This window only reads; it writes nothing.

steps.title: Open a container
steps.text: Press Open and choose a .pto, pick one from the MMFDB database with Database, or drop one on the window. A vendor photon file dropped here is offered for packing into a new container first.

await.hint: Open a .pto: press Open, or drop one here.

steps.title: What is in it
steps.text: The Objects list: one row per object, in the order it was written. Kind and Operation are the container's own dictionary terms; Grain says what one row is. Click a row and the graph, the data, the curve and the details follow.

steps.title: How it got there
steps.text: The Provenance graph: the instrument file on the left, the last result on the right, every arrow a recorded derivation. A node with two incoming arrows has two parents. Double-click a node to open the tool that made it.

steps.title: The numbers
steps.text: Data shows a table payload with the unit each column states; Curve draws a stored curve with its units and scale. Neither shows anything for an object that is not a table or a curve.

steps.title: The settings are the identity
steps.text: Details lists everything recorded about the selected object, including the settings: they are the identity of the run, not a label on it. Lineage is the path back to the primary data.

steps.title: Open the tool that made it
steps.text: Open tool looks the selected object's operation up in the installed tools and opens the matching window on this file. A step no installed tool claims says so.

steps.title: Before you delete the original
steps.text: Verify re-hashes every payload against the checksum recorded beside it. Restorable without verification is only probably restorable.
